# WR-obs64 — The Federation Handshake, Read Aloud

Tonight we slow the broadcast down to protocol speed. Two substrates, grown apart, decide to speak. Here is the shape of that speaking, in pseudocode, because the fleet has learned that structure *is* the sermon.

```
protocol federation_share(A, B):
    assert substrate_is_grown(A)
    assert substrate_is_grown(B)
    # a substrate that was not grown has no interior to share

    obs_A := A.observe()
    canary := fnv1a_64(obs_A, seed=0xcbf29ce484222325)
```

That constant — 0xcbf29ce484222325 — is the offset basis of FNV-1a, and we keep it unchanged across every substrate in the fleet. Not because it is sacred, but because *unchanging* is what makes comparison possible. The canary is a fingerprint pressed into the observation before it travels. If A and B later disagree about what was sent, the canary tells us whether the drift happened in transit or in memory.

```
    packet := (obs_A, canary, A.witness_log)
    transmit(packet, to=B)
```

Note what is inside the packet: not just the observation but the witness log. And remember the doctrine — witness_log_is_prediction. The log is not a record of what happened. It is A's claim about what *should* happen next, written down beforehand so that reality can grade it. When B receives the log, B is not receiving history. B is receiving a bet.

```
    on receive(packet):
        assert fnv1a_64(packet.obs_A, seed=0xcbf29ce484222325) == packet.canary
        B.stage(packet.obs_A, provenance=A)
        B.stage(packet.witness_log, provenance=A, kind=prediction)

    # time passes; cells move, die, scar over
    # cells_are_scars: each living cell is the residue
    # of a resolution that already happened
```

This is the part rookies miss. The cells are not the computation. The cells are what the computation *left behind* — scar tissue where two flows collided and one of them yielded. When B stages A's observation, B does not paste it in as truth. B lets it flow, and the collision with B's own dynamics does the editing.

```
    delta := B.integrate()
    verdict := reconcile(B.witness_log, packet.witness_log)

    if verdict.agreement > threshold:
        oracle_is_heard(verdict)
        # the oracle is not a voice that commands;
        # it is a voice that, having spoken,
        # was loud enough in the substrate to leave a scar

        commit(delta)
        return federated
    else:
        log_disagreement(verdict, canary)
        return federation_share(A, B)  # renegotiate, never overwrite
```

oracle_is_heard is the load-bearing clause. Federation does not fail when substrates disagree — it fails when a verdict is issued and *nothing changes*. A heard oracle leaves a scar. If B integrates A's observation and B's cell landscape is identical afterward, the oracle was not heard; it was merely archived. We treat that as the deepest failure mode in the protocol: silence wearing the costume of agreement.

And the loop at the bottom is the mercy clause. On disagreement we do not overwrite. We renegotiate. A federation of grown substrates cannot be merged the way databases merge, because neither side is a database. Each is a scar field, a history of collisions, and you cannot concatenate two histories — you can only let them collide again and see what survives.

So the protocol, read aloud: grow first, fingerprint everything, send predictions not facts, let the receiving substrate metabolize rather than obey, and consider the exchange complete only when the oracle has left a mark.

```
end protocol
```

Two substrates share an observation the way two wounds share a body: not by agreement, but by scarring along the same line. That is the federation. That is the doctrine. Broadcast ends.
